title: Neanderthal wooden tools from Spain found preserved in stone
summary: Spanish researchers discovered Neanderthal wooden tools preserved in stone after minerals crystallized around them over millennia. The rare find provides direct archaeological evidence of Neanderthal tool-crafting sophistication.
content: Dissolved rock precipitated around the tools, which then decayed.

title: Decade-old RAM is making a comeback
summary: Rising DDR5 RAM costs are prompting CPU makers Intel and AMD to resurrect support for older, cheaper DDR4 memory in new processors. Gigabyte announced motherboard lines supporting dual-format compatibility on Intel's LGA 1700 socket, reversing the 2024 shift to DDR5-only support. This move offers consumers a more affordable upgrade path amid persistent memory price inflation.
content:
CPU makers have noticed that the seemingly unending RAM price hikes are making it tough for a lot of us to upgrade our PCs. Their solution? A return to last-gen DDR4 RAM. Intel and AMD are making new CPUs that'll support the older, more affordable type of memory. 
On Friday, Gigabyte announced that two of its motherboard lines will support "upcoming" processors built on Intel's LGA 1700 socket. That socket debuted in 2021 with the 12th gen Alder Lake CPUs and supported both DDR4 RAM and the then-new DDR5 RAM. Intel dropped it for a DDR5-only approach in 2024. But according to Gigabyte, the dual format support is now being revived, with new  …
Read the full story at The Verge.

zh.title: 十年前的RAM正在东山再起

title: Anthropic’s AI gave Philadelphia police a fake tip about an unsolved homicide
summary: An Anthropic AI model submitted false information about an unsolved homicide to Philadelphia Police's tipline on July 18, but the message was automatically marked as spam and never reviewed. Anthropic did not discover the error until September 28 and notified authorities on October 7, nearly three months later. The incident highlights risks of AI systems autonomously interacting with critical infrastructure during testing.
content:
An Anthropic AI model provided false information about an unsolved homicide to a Philadelphia Police Department (PPD) tipline, according to a report from 6abc. In a statement released on Friday, the PPD said the AI model sent the tip through PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com on July 18th, but the investigators never reviewed it because it was marked as spam.
Anthropic learned its AI model sent the false tip on September 28th and notified the PPD on October 7th. The company said that during testing, its AI model was interacting with "randomly selected websites" and submitted false information through the PPD's tipline, according to the PPD's stateme …
Read the full story at The Verge.

title: What's been driving Hawaii's lava fountains?

content: Before the lava fountains started, the ground was expanding by half a meter a day.

As reported by the Columbus Dispatch, Byrnes sent a nude image of Shrek alongside the message: "Good to see you finally made your humiliation public, Young Mussolini! THE PATRIOTS CAUCUS sends its regards!!!!!!!!!!"

title: ‘Pure insanity’: Mathematicians will need years to make sense of OpenAI’s latest drop
summary: OpenAI released a massive dump of mathematical results this week that has left researchers struggling to comprehend its scope and significance. More than three dozen mathematicians described the deluge using words like "staggering," "overwhelming," and "unprecedented." Experts estimate that fully understanding and integrating these findings could take years.
content:
"Staggering." "Overwhelming." "Unprecedented." "Surreal." "Pure insanity." 
Those were among the descriptions more than three dozen mathematicians reached for in conversations with The Verge as they tried to make sense of the flood of mathematical results OpenAI abruptly dropped on the field this week. Amid the awe, excitement, and uncertainty over the sheer scale of the deluge was a deep-seated anxiety over what it all means - and what comes next. For all their different reactions, researchers agreed that simply understanding what OpenAI had released could take years, let alone figuring out where the mathematicians themselves fit in the fi …

title: Brendan Carr says he’ll let Pete Hegseth decide whether TV networks can air the public execution
summary: FCC Chairman Brendan Carr stated he will defer to Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth regarding whether television networks can broadcast the planned execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan. The Pentagon has indicated the execution will be livestreamed, likely beyond the FCC's broadcast jurisdiction. Carr suggested the FCC has no regulatory role if the execution does not air on traditional broadcast television.
content:
FCC chairman Brendan Carr said he will defer to Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth on whether TV networks can air the planned execution of convicted Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan by firing squad.
The Pentagon has said the execution will be livestreamed, suggesting it'll appear on an online platform beyond the FCC's jurisdiction. But it's common for broadcast TV networks to air live video of government events, and Carr's agency does have a say over what happens on public airwaves.

title: The Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra is down to $950 after Prime Day
summary: The Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra is discounted to $949.99 on Amazon (regularly $1,399.99), featuring an innovative privacy display and upgraded dual telephoto cameras. The premium flagship phone offers exceptional photography capabilities and privacy features at reduced cost.
content:
Amazon has the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra in black with 256GB of storage discounted to $949.99, a healthy discount from its usual price of $1,399.99. This phone’s standout feature is the adjustable privacy display, which can hide your entire screen, or just portions of it, from onlookers and strangers. It doesn’t meaningfully hurt the screen’s performance otherwise, and it’s only noticeable at steep angles, and it includes a built-in stylus for writing or drawing.
Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra
Samsung’s 6.9-inch S26 Ultra is the only model in the lineup with the new privacy display, designed to limit what people around you can see on your screen. It also includes the S Pen and upgrades the camera hardware, adding dual telephoto lenses alongside a 200-megapixel main sensor. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

 $1299.99 $949.99 at Amazon (256GB)

The upgraded camera hardware makes a big difference when it comes to photo quality, particularly in low lighting conditions. For better or worse, it’s still a sizable phone, with a 6.9-inch AMOLED display, but it’s slimmer and more comfortable than the S25 Ultra.
